'''''Paleoagave''''' is a genus of [[flowering plant]]s in the family [[Asparagaceae]]. It includes a single species, '''''Paleoagave bracteosa''''' ([[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] ''Agave bracteosa'') which commonly known as '''spider agave''' or '''squid agave'''. It is native to the [[Sierra Madre Oriental]] of northeastern [[Mexico]] (spanning the states of [[Tamaulipas]], [[Coahuila]] and [[Nuevo León]]).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Agave bracteosa at San Marcos Growers |url=https://www.smgrowers.com/products/plants/plantdisplay.asp?plant_id=2037 |access-date=16 May 2024}}</ref> 

==Description==
Small among the agaves, its green and succulent leaves are long and [[lanceolate]], 50–70 cm long and 3–5 cm at the base, where they are the widest. Compared to the larger, more formidable agaves, they have minute [[serration]]s (teeth) along the margins but neither teeth, nor terminal spine, at the leaf tip. The leaves have a tendency to curl somewhat, in a fashion reminiscent of the octopus agave ''[[Agave vilmoriniana|A. vilmoriniana]]''. The inflorescence spike is also short, at 1.2–1.7 meters, and its upper-third is densely covered with white or pale-yellow flowers. The flowers are distinctive, in that [[tepal]]s arise from a disk-shaped [[Receptacle (botany)|receptacle]] rather than the usual tube. The [[stamens]] are quite long.<ref>[[Howard Scott Gentry]], ''Agaves of Continental North America'' (University of Arizona Press, 1982) pp. 91-93</ref>

==Taxonomy==
The species was first described as ''Agave bracteosa'' by [[Sereno Watson]] in 1882, and placed in the large genus ''[[Agave]]''.<ref name = powo/> [[Howard Scott Gentry|Gentry]] defined a group "Choritepalae" that includes ''A. bracteosa'' along with ''[[Agave ellemeetiana]]'' and ''[[Agave guiengola]]'', and states that the [[wikt:discoid|discoid]] [[Receptacle (botany)|receptacle]] and unarmed leaves are different enough from other agaves to justify placing ''A. bracteosa'' and ''A. ellemeetiana'' into a separate genus, but the characteristics of ''A. guiengola'' link the group to the rest of ''Agave''.{{cn|date=July 2026}}

==Distribution and habitat==
It grows in well-drained and bright but shaded or protected locations, such as under trees or on cliffs or rocky slopes (facing away from the sun). The species can be found growing between 900 and 1700 meters elevation (from 2,950' ft. up to nearly 5,500') above sea level.<ref>Engelmann, Georg, Garden Chronicles 2:18, 776, fig 138, 139. 1882.</ref> 

==Conservation==
Although it occupies a small range, it is not considered to be threatened.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />
